acceptanceCriteria: A process-exit path (os.Exit after an adapter watchdog or dogfood event deadline) kills every live child process group the adapter started, including git spawned by gokernel, gitstatus and contextindex, before exiting.
TestAHI044HookAdaptersFailOpen's slow-git case reports Git outliving the adapter by under 100 ms across -count=5, and the outlived bound is asserted rather than logged.
No new daemon, no login shell, and no change to the hook exit status or stdout contract.
body: Observed 2026-10-04 while building V1-0711 (AHI-044 fail-open matrix, branch claude/v1-0711-fail-open-matrix, base be98482b). When the adapter watchdog or dogfood event deadline abandons a git read and main calls os.Exit, exec's asynchronous context Cancel (process-group SIGKILL, internal/gokernel/process_unix.go) has not run yet, so the git child and its descendants survive the adapter. Reproduction: go test -count=3 -run TestAHI044 ./cmd/corvint/ with the slow-git PATH shim (logs pid, /bin/sleep 5, exec real git). Observed: 'Git outlived the adapter by' 3.763s and 3.772s (codex Stop / slow git on PATH) and 4.801s (claude-code session-end / slow git on PATH); every other case 0-43 ms. Expected: no child outlives the adapter process. Impact is bounded: the reads use --no-optional-locks and V1-0711 removes the private status scratch at exit (gitstatus.CloseScratch), but a hung real git would keep running after the host considers the hook finished. Spawn sites with Setpgid are many (gokernel, contextindex, cem/gitrun, worksource, ...), so the fix is a shared live-group registry consulted at exit, analogous to gitstatus.CloseScratch.

title: hosts: git children abandoned by an adapter deadline outlive the adapter because os.Exit beats exec's group kill
